cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Back My Version
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to remember, repeat, and defend one shared version of events when questions begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The caretaker's asking about our extra key. Tell him we were checking the cake cupboard's lock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We did check it. Then we ate the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Start with the part we both remember as maintenance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll ask why there are crumbs in the lock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we both remember a blockage. Say that back so we're consistent.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts the crumbs into the object of supposed maintenance and demands a rehearsal.

specificity.evidence: A1 caretaker, key and cake cupboard establish the immediate cover-story task.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 blockage is an earned reinterpretation of B4 crumbs rather than an unrelated excuse.
